name: Data.Pair.ratio_ne_zero_and_real
summary: Both partial L-values are non-zero at z (`AutChar.HasWeight.L_ne_zero`); a quotient of absolute values is real.

steps.claim: Not a step of the proof: lines 125–126 are the rest of the statement, which ends before the `:=` on line 126 (a second-reader message). The line census takes the `:=` of `let r :=` on line 125 for the start of the value, so the check requires these lines to be owned here. They state: with r = ratio(p, ϑ, s): r ≠ 0 ∧ conj r = r.
steps.lean:
p.ratio ϑ s; r ≠ 0 ∧ star r =
    r := by

steps.claim: The partial L-values L(z, (νϑ^s)⁻¹) and L(z, ν⁻¹) are non-zero (`AutChar.HasWeight.L_ne_zero`, for the characters of the given weights at the point z of the pair), so r ≠ 0; r is a quotient of real numbers, so real.
steps.lean:
simp (disch := simp [funext_iff] <;> grind [p.8 1, Pair]) [ratio,
  ((ϑ.4.zpow s).inv.mul p.hasWeight.inv).L_ne_zero, p.hasWeight.inv.L_ne_zero]
